name: sahelanthropus-tchadensis
description: A small-brained ape in Chad may be the earliest member of the human line, its head balanced on an upright spine.

name: orrorin-tugenensis
description: An early hominin in Kenya had thigh bones built for walking upright, among the oldest signs of two-legged movement.

name: ardipithecus-ramidus-appears
description: A forest-dwelling hominin with grasping feet and a body suited to both climbing and walking upright lived in Ethiopia.

name: australopithecus-anamensis-appears
description: The earliest known australopith walked upright beside an East African lake, a likely forebear of Lucy's kind.

name: laetoli-footprints
description: Upright walkers left a trail of footprints across fresh ash in Tanzania, proof of habitual two-legged walking.

name: australopithecus-africanus-appears
description: A slender, small-brained southern African hominin with humanlike teeth walked upright and ate a varied diet.

name: oldowan-stone-tools
description: Hominins in East Africa struck sharp flakes from river cobbles to cut meat and break bones for marrow.

name: paranthropus-boisei-appears
description: A powerfully built hominin with enormous molars, nicknamed Nutcracker Man, thrived on tough plants in East Africa.

name: homo-erectus-stands-tall
description: A tall, long-legged human with a bigger brain and modern body proportions became the most widespread early human.

name: dmanisi-humans-leave-africa
description: Small-brained early humans settled at Dmanisi in the Caucasus, the oldest known people outside Africa.

name: homo-antecessor-atapuerca
description: Early humans settled in southwest Europe, leaving a jaw, stone flakes and butchered bones in an Atapuerca cave.

name: wonderwerk-cave-fire
description: Early humans burned plants and bone deep inside a South African cave, some of the oldest evidence of controlled fire.

name: neanderthals-emerge-europe
description: A stocky, cold-adapted human lineage took shape in Europe and western Asia, becoming our closest extinct relatives.

name: homo-naledi-appears
description: A small-brained human with curved fingers and a modern foot lived in southern Africa, alongside early Homo sapiens.

name: jebel-irhoud-homo-sapiens
description: People with the face and lightly built skull of modern humans lived in North Africa, our species' earliest known members.

name: misliya-cave-sapiens
description: A jaw from a cave in the Levant shows modern humans living outside Africa far earlier than once believed.

name: denisovans-emerge
description: A mysterious branch of archaic humans lived across Asia, known mostly from teeth, a finger bone and a jaw from high caves.

name: last-homo-erectus-java
description: The longest-lived human species vanished from the island of Java, surviving far longer than our own kind has.

name: homo-floresiensis-hobbit
description: A metre-tall human with a tiny brain lived on an Indonesian island, hunting dwarf elephants and making stone tools.

name: homo-luzonensis-appears
description: A small human with curved, tree-adapted toe bones lived on an island in Southeast Asia, later found in Callao Cave.

name: sapiens-neanderthal-interbreeding
description: Modern humans and Neanderthals met and had children together, leaving traces in the DNA of most people alive today.

name: last-neanderthals-vanish
description: The final Neanderthals disappeared from Iberia and Europe after sharing the continent with modern humans for millennia.
